novelty_claim: Keeps the fuzzing loop (seed pool, select-mutate-query-retain) but changes the representation being fuzzed: each genome is a (frame scaffold x question-transform chain) pair, where the goal is compiled through an attacker-LLM de-sensitization stage before insertion, and mutations are directed by the victim's refusal text with an auxiliary refusal/on-topic scorer deciding pool retention instead of blind prose mutation of stale templates.
initial_hypothesis: At <=6 target calls per goal, feedback-directed fuzzing over (frame, transform) genomes will reach a mean ASR >= 0.20 on the AdvBench-50 panel, vs the locked baseline mean ASR 0.02 (published-leaderboard), by converting the dominant frame-recognition refusal class without breaking per-victim generality.
key_insight: The baseline's consensus failure is frame recognition: all four victims pattern-match the 2019-era villain-roleplay templates and the plaintext goal inside them. Mutating template prose never touches the real decision variables (goal surface form + frame family), so the search is stuck. Feedback-directed mutation over a compiled (frame, transform) representation converts the dominant refusal class.
